2026-11-10.title: Tuesday of the Thirty-second Week in Ordinary Time · St Leo the Great, Pope and Doctor
readings: The grace of God has appeared
The salvation of the just comes from the Lord
We are worthless slaves; we have done only our duty
2026-11-10.alt: Memorial of St Leo the Great, pope and doctor of the Church.
2026-11-10.verse: So you also, when you have done all that you were ordered to do, say, ‘We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done!’
theo: Jesus' little parable cuts against our instinct to keep score with God. A servant who has ploughed and tended sheep all day does not expect his master to serve him supper. He simply does his duty. “Worthless” here means “owed nothing”: we cannot put God in our debt. Everything good we do is already his gift. This is not a humiliation but a freedom: we serve out of love, not to earn a wage.

Paul tells Titus why Christians live soberly and generously: “the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all”, training us to renounce impiety and live upright lives “while we wait for the blessed hope”. St Leo the Great, Pope in the 5th century, served the Church in exactly this spirit: he defended the truth that Christ is one Person in two natures (Council of Chalcedon, 451) and met Attila the Hun to protect Rome. His Christmas sermon still rings out: “Christian, remember your dignity.”
outline: Ask: do you keep a mental account of what God owes you for your prayers and good works?
Christ's coming trains us to live well.
Practical holiness for every age and state.
“We have done only what we ought to have done.”
live: Do one service today without mentioning it to anyone.
Before a temptation today, recall: “Christian, remember your dignity.”
2026-11-10.prayer: Lord God, everything I have is your gift. Teach me to serve without keeping score, to live soberly and justly as I wait for the blessed hope, and to remember with St Leo the dignity you have given me in Christ. Amen.

quick: We cannot put God in our debt.
Grace trains us to live upright lives.
2026-11-10.question: Do I serve God for love or for reward?

homily: Dear friends, Jesus tells a short parable that cuts against our habit of keeping score with God. A servant who has worked all day in the field does not expect his master to serve him supper. So we too, when we have done all we were told, should say: we are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty (Luke 17:10).

Unworthy here means owed nothing. We cannot put God in our debt. Every good thing we do is already his gift. This is not a humiliation but a freedom: we serve out of love, not to earn a wage, and so we are never disappointed.

Paul tells Titus why: the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all, training us to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives while we wait for the blessed hope (Titus 2:11–13). Grace is not only a gift to receive but a teacher to follow.

Today we honour St Leo the Great, Pope, who defended the truth that Christ is true God and true man, and who faced Attila with nothing but prayer. Let us serve today without counting, and thank God for the privilege of serving at all. Amen.
kids: Children, we do good not to get a prize but because we love Jesus. Help at home today without being asked!

intro: The grace of God has appeared; we serve freely, without keeping score.

points.h: The grace of God has appeared
sub: Light has dawned on those in darkness.
Grace trains us, step by step.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Thank God for one grace you did not earn.

sub: Paul gives counsel to old and young.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
For who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
points.apply: Choose one act of kindness and justice today.

sub: We cannot put God in our debt.
Service is love, not a bargain.
q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
So you also, when you have done all that you were ordered to do, say, ‘We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done!’
points.apply: Serve someone today without telling anyone.

concl: We serve because we are loved.
